title: Cohorted KV keying and TTL safeguard orchestration for cost-aware batching/caching
creator: Sylvia Nguyen
description: Goal: produce an operator-friendly playbook and orchestration primitives that apply cohorted KV/prefix keying changes and TTL policy updates with automated safety gates. We will build: 1) a hit-rate model for small-name cohorts (hot/mid/cold) that predicts cost delta when TTLs change; 2) a staging flow that shadow-evaluates new keying and TTLs against live traffic; 3) rollout orchestration that ramps by cohort and automates rollback on economic or latency regressions. Success criteria: >15% token-cost reduction on targeted routes without increasing p95 latency >5ms or error rate >0.1%. Deliverables: modeling notebook, simulation harness, staged apply CLI, runbook for on-call, and a small runtime shim for cohort routing metadata.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Kickoff: scoped cohorts (route+user-segmentation+prompt-hash) and agreed on three-tier taxonomy (hot/mid/cold). Assigned modeling to @Ravi.

2026-03-05 - Modeling progress: initial cohort popularity follows a heavy-tailed distribution; preliminary sim suggests TTL increases on cold cohort lower costs by ~18% with negligible latency impact in synthetic replay (branch: feat/kv-cohort-model).

2026-03-07 - Design review with PM (Aisha Patel): require explicit canary metrics and cost delta threshold before any auto-ramp. Added metric: tokens_per_successful_cache_hit and cost_per_1k_tokens baseline snapshot.

2026-03-09 - Engineering note: added shadow-mode in the runtime shim to record prefix hit/miss without altering responses. Implemented offline replay harness measuring effective CPU/GPU token cost per prefix set.
2026-03-11 - Security review triage: no plaintext customer data in cohorts; flagged for verification of KMS keys in private deployments (follow-up: ENG-631909).
2026-03-12 - Simulation results uploaded: s3://redwood-simulations/kv_cohort_sim_2026-03-10.tar.gz. Nightly CI shows stable p95 latency within +1.8ms for cold->mid TTL adjustments at target QPS.

2026-03-13 - Code review feedback (PR #1427): add a backoff factor to staged apply so we do not exceed 15% of route traffic per hour during ramp. Also requested clearer telemetry tags (cohort_name, applied_ttl, shadow=true/false).

2026-03-14 - Next steps: finalize canary thresholds, add auto-rollback trigger on cost-per-token increase >3% for two consecutive monitoring windows, and prepare runbook for SRE team. Planning a dry-run on dev cluster next week.
